description: This is a team that aims at learning something new each project while it brings creativity and innovation to the table.
summary: FireVisor is a web-app that uses NASA’s data to prevent or be able to control fires all over the world. Our goal is to create an interactive web-app so people can stay alerted to fires and be able to respond before it spreads and gets out of control. We know fires can’t be predictable, but they can be controlled before it burns everything. We develop a web-app that analyzes and compares wildfires from different years and seasons to send alerts and enable people to take precautions in the event of a new wildfire. It also looks for weather anomalies to warn of a potential wildfire. We use NASA FIRMS as our primary data source, as well as Python and JavaScript, which help us compare the data. In our project, we combine MODIS with VIIRS, which gives us greater accuracy in identifying dry areas prone to wildfires.
details:
FireVisor is an interactive map that alerts users to dry conditions prone to fires or fires that are already active. It works by selecting a region and estimated dates, then it compares fires in that area, helping us to make a prediction of a future fire. It also helps to monitor how a fire spreads, allowing people in the area to avoid being near the fire and enabling firefighters to act as preventively as possible. The benefits of this website include the ability to prevent structural damage, loss of life, and long-term fire spread. The goal is to prevent any harm that might be suffered by people, as well as damage to their homes, animals, etc.

Our code is based on Python and JavaScript, and Codex helped us structure it better and streamline the calibration between MODIS and VIIRS. Other tools that help us were MapLibre, WebGL, SQLite, NASA Earthdata, GWIS/JRC, and Meteomatics Weather; they mostly help us on the map, data, etc. We take into account the data coming from the MODIS and VIIRS sensors and the patterns that have been analyzed over the past few years, so that we can compare information and reach new conclusions.

Our project uses many different technologies to solve a major problem in a way that everyone can use; our creativity was focused on making it effective and accessible to all. We know this web-app can help everyone, especially in areas where drought is leading to an increasing number of fires. Therefore, we aim for our impact to be global and primarily focused on firefighters, farmers in fire-prone areas, or people who want to prevent the loss of family members, pets, homes, etc.
